data.pni_summary: What could happen if something goes wrong? When your *Privacy Not Included researcher wanted to get a fitness tracking smartwatch to see how stressed out reading privacy policies made her, Garmin is what she went with. Because Garmin seems to do one of the best jobs handling the privacy and security of all the personal data fitness trackers collect, at least according to their really not that stressful privacy policy . (Seriously, companies who have privacy policies, please, look to Garmin as an example of how to do privacy practices and policies right.) Here’s what this privacy researcher really likes about Garmin. Yes, Garmin's fitness trackers and smartwatches can collect a whole lot of personal information through the device and on the Garmin Connect app . That’s what a fitness trackers and smartwatch are designed to do, that's why we want them. Garmin says they can collect data like email address, device information, location, and all that body-related data like physical activity, stress, sleep patterns, heat rate, pulse ox, and more. Here's the thing. Garmin might collect lots of data, but they then do a pretty good job, as far as we can tell, of respecting it, protecting it, and not trying to make money off sharing or selling it. Gasp! What a wonderful idea. Your “sharing with others” user settings in the Garmin Connect app are set to “private” by default. Which is great. events.verdict_md: Garmin's Venu 3 collects a wide range of personal data, including name, address, location information, speed, direction, device usage frequency, and biometric data such as physical activity, stress, sleep patterns, heart rate, and pulse ox. This data is shared with subsidiaries and affiliates, strategic partners, co-branded sites, third-party application providers, marketing partners, service providers, law enforcement, and public authorities. The scariest clause is that Garmin may disclose personal identifiable information (PII) to law enforcement and public authorities under applicable law, legal process, or to protect rights, privacy, safety, or property. Garmin has a good track record with no reported breaches.
tips: Be cautious when sharing personal data with third-party applications and services.
Review and adjust your privacy settings in the Garmin Connect app to ensure you are not sharing more data than you intend to.
Consider opting out of receiving marketing-related emails and sharing PII with third parties for their marketing purposes.
